## The Code Itself

Both functions appear together in MLflow's span entity source code (`mlflow/entities/span.py`). They're invoked when a span is being ended, as part of the finalization logic. The relevant snippet shows: if the status code is not ERROR, the status is set to OK, and then if `should_compute_cost_client_side()` returns true, `set_span_cost_attribute(self)` is called before applying span processors and ending the underlying OpenTelemetry span.

In short, `should_compute_cost_client_side()` is a gating check that determines whether cost should be calculated on the client rather than the server, and `set_span_cost_attribute()` performs the actual client-side cost computation and attaches it as an attribute to the span.

## Why Client-Side Computation Exists

The distinction between client-side and server-side cost computation is tied to different deployment scenarios. According to MLflow's documentation, when using Databricks managed MLflow, the cost computation requires the client application to install the necessary dependencies. This contrasts with the self-hosted setup, where to enable cost tracking you need to start the MLflow Tracking Server with the [genai] extra installed, and it is recommended to start your MLflow server with the extra installed even if you don't need cost tracking.

## Related Context on Cost Tracking

This client-side/server-side logic supports MLflow's broader cost-tracking feature. MLflow automatically extracts model information from LLM spans and calculates costs, with a UI that renders model and cost data directly in trace views, and costs are aggregated and broken down in the "Overview" tab. This cost data is available at both the span level (individual LLM calls) and aggregated at the trace level.
